draft.title: How government uses behavioural insights
card: A nudge is a small change to how a choice is set up that steers people towards a better outcome. It does not ban any option or force anyone.
Default
the option people get if they do nothing. Many people stick with it, so opt-out superannuation enrols workers unless they choose to leave.
Reminder
a message sent at the right time, such as an SMS about an overdue fine or a health check, which helps people act when they might forget.
Presentation
how options are laid out, such as listing a preferred choice first on a form, which can shift what people pick.
draft.remember: Nudges steer choices through defaults, reminders and layout, and people can still choose otherwise.

a.q: A state government changes a form so that people are enrolled as organ donors unless they tick a box to opt out. Which nudge is this?
opts: A default
A reminder
A ban on opting out
A tax on not donating
a.why: Being enrolled is what happens if people do nothing, so it is a default. It is not a ban, because people can still tick the box and leave.
a.clue: What happens if a person does nothing?

b.q: A council in Victoria sends an SMS a week before dog registration is due. Why is this a nudge rather than a rule?
opts: It prompts action but leaves the choice with people
It bans owners from skipping the registration
It makes registration cheaper for every owner
It gives owners more information about the rules
b.why: The SMS steers people to act on time and removes no option. A rule or ban would force the outcome. The message does not change the price, so cost is not the reason.
b.clue: Does the message take any choice away?

b.best: It prompts action but leaves the choice with people

problems.detail: 'Opt-out superannuation enrols workers unless they choose to leave' is not true in Australia. Superannuation Guarantee contributions are compulsory, so workers cannot leave super. The Australian default is being placed in a default (MySuper or stapled) fund unless they choose another fund. The example should describe defaulting into a fund, not opting out of super.

Dog registration is compulsory by law in Victoria, so saying the SMS 'leaves the choice with people' could teach students that registering is optional. The question should make clear that the reminder itself adds no new rule or penalty, or it should use a voluntary action.

check.summary: The card's superannuation example is wrong for Australia, where workers cannot opt out of super, only choose a fund other than the default. Question b's dog registration example blurs a legally compulsory action with a free choice.

card: A nudge is a small change to how a choice is set up that steers people towards a better outcome. It does not ban any option or force anyone.
Default
the option people get if they do nothing, and many people stick with it. Workers who do not pick a super fund are placed in a default fund, but they can choose another.
Reminder
a message sent at the right time, such as an SMS about an overdue fine or a health check, which helps people act when they might forget.
Presentation
how options are laid out, such as listing a preferred choice first on a form, which can shift what people pick.
proposal.remember: Nudges steer choices through defaults, reminders and layout, and people can still choose otherwise.

a.q: A state government changes a form so that people are enrolled as organ donors unless they tick a box to opt out. Which nudge is this?
opts: A default
A reminder
A ban on opting out
A tax on not donating
a.why: Being enrolled is what happens if people do nothing, so it is a default. It is not a ban, because people can still tick the box and leave.
a.clue: What happens if a person does nothing?

b.q: A health department sends people an SMS saying their free flu jab is now available. Why is this a nudge rather than a rule?
opts: It prompts action without removing any option
It sets the flu jab as the default choice
It makes the flu jab compulsory for adults
It fines people who choose to skip the jab
b.why: The SMS helps people act when they might forget, and they can still say no, so it is a reminder nudge. It is not a default, because nobody is booked in if they do nothing. A fine or a legal duty would force the outcome, which a nudge does not do.
b.clue: What happens to a person who ignores the message?

b.best: It prompts action without removing any option
